function: Constrained DRL jointly chooses cooperative beamformers, BS selection and movable-antenna positions to minimize transmit power under worst-case rate and sensing HCRLB constraints in cooperative ISAC (pp. 6-7).
system: C-ISAC with B=3 BSs, each a UPA of N=8 transmit and M=4 sensing receive movable antennas; U=2 single-antenna users, one target; no RIS; frequency not stated (pp. 3, 8).
method: Constrained DRL: primal-dual DDPG actor-critic with Wolpertinger action selection; trained offline in simulation, trained actor then used online; reinforcement learning (pp. 7-8).
data_channel: Self-built field-response channels, 3 paths, path loss PL0=-30 dB at 1 m with exponents 2.8 and 2.2; fixed node positions (Fig. 3); no dataset (pp. 3, 8).
test_conditions: Agent trained and evaluated in one simulated C-ISAC setup (B=3, U=2, Fig. 3); sweeps over CSI error, TS error, number of MAs and BSs (pp. 8-10).
baselines: SDR-based and ZF-based beamforming (classical); FPA and APS antenna schemes (solver not stated); no earlier learned method or DRL baseline compared (pp. 9-10).
metrics: Average transmit power (dBm), cumulative reward and cost over episodes, number of BSs needed, under worst-case rate and HCRLB constraints (pp. 8-10).
complexity: Order of the actor forward pass in online use: O(N1 (N B U + N M B) N3^2 N2^2 + N5^2 N4); no runtime or parameter count (p. 7).
q1_support: p. 3: "Based on the field response channel model [24]"; p. 8: "the positions of the BSs, users, and targets are shown in Fig.3"; a custom channel with its own path loss, not a standardized or measured model.
q2_support: p. 8: "In the simulation, the positions of the BSs, users, and targets are shown in Fig.3, where B = 3, U = 2, and T = 1"; the paper describes one setup with sweeps and no test in a scenario unseen in training.
q3_support: p. 9: "with existing beamforming methods based on semidefinite relaxation (SDR) and zero-forcing (ZF)"; p. 9: "the Adaptive Portable Antenna (APS) scheme, and the FPA scheme"; no earlier learned method is compared.
q4_support: p. 7: "complexity in the forward pass of the actor-network in online deployment"
q5_support: p. 8: "In the simulation, the positions of the BSs, users, and targets are shown in Fig.3"; the paper gives no code or data link and uses no public dataset.
notes: PDF is the arXiv version 2501.15410v1 (26 Jan 2025). Page 1 shows no DOI, so the match with 10.1109/tcomm.2025.3648983 rests on title and content only; nothing contradicts it. Area 5: the learned agent sets beamformers in an ISAC system, together with antenna positions and BS selection. The single-antenna exclusion does not apply: each BS has 8 transmit and 4 receive movable antennas. In this version the captions of Figs. 4 and 8 are swapped with their content (the BS-count bars are on p. 8, the reward and cost curves on p. 10). q3 is 0 because SDR, ZF, FPA and APS are the only comparisons; p. 7 says only that DQN struggles with large action spaces, with no DRL baseline run. q4 rests on the order of the actor forward pass.
